Document: Schedule for Payment of Hostel Fees by On-Roll UG, PG & Ph.D Students for Autumn Semester 2026-27
Reference No: HCU/Hostel Fees/UG-PG/Autumn/2026-27
Date: 30.04.2026

All on-roll Undergraduate, Postgraduate and Ph.D students are required to pay their Hostel Fees for Autumn 2026-27 as per the following schedule.

026

All on-roll Undergraduate, Postgraduate and Ph.D students are required to pay their Hostel Fees for Autumn 2026-27 as per the following schedule.

PAYMENT SCHEDULE:
- Payment of Hostel Fees for Autumn Semester 2026-27: 01.05.2026 to 15.07.2026
- Payment of 1st installment of Semester Mess Advance (SMA) for Autumn Semester 2026-27: 01.05.2026 to 15.07.2026
- Payment of 2nd installment of SMA for Autumn Semester 2026-27: On/Before 30.09.2026
- Payment of Hostel Fees with fine of Rs.100/- per day: After 15.07.2026, a fine of Rs.100/- per day will be charged w.e.f. 16.07.2026 till the date of payment of Hostel Fees.
- Payment of 1st installment of SMA with fine of Rs.100/- per day: After 15.07.2026, a fine of Rs.100/- per day will be charged w.e.f. 16.07.2026 till the date of payment of SMA.
- Payment of 2nd installment of SMA with fine of Rs.100/- per day: After 30.09.2026, a fine of Rs.100/- per day will be charged w.e.f. 01.10.2026 till the date of payment of SMA.

PAYMENT PROCESS NOTES:
- All students (including students paying through a Bank Loan/Sponsoring Agency) need to pay fees using the "Online Portal" (https://portal.iitb.ac.in/asc).
- Instructions for online Hostel Fee payment are on the ASC home page (https://portal.iitb.ac.in/asc). Students paying fee through portal (online mode) must ensure that their transaction is completed in all respects.
- Bank Loan / Sponsorship / NEFT: The official Fee Demand for such students, to pay the fees directly to IIT Bombay Bank Account, will have to be generated on ASC Portal only (Bank Loan / NEFT fee payment tab at https://portal.iitb.ac.in/asc).
  a) A demand will be valid for 10 days only, before which the money has to be transferred. In case of delays expected from the agency transferring the fees, a fresh demand has to be generated.
  b) Once the money has been transferred, the student must enter

expected from the agency transferring the fees, a fresh demand has to be generated.
  b) Once the money has been transferred, the student must enter the UTR number and other details on the ASC portal.
  c) Initiate the payment process with the agency at least 15 days prior to the fees deadline as it takes a few days for reconciliation from the bank. Semester registration is linked to fee payment.
  d) Students must not intimate IIT Bombay by email, as done during July 2025 and earlier. Only online fees demand and UTR entry will be entertained henceforth.

The fee receipt will be generated after reconciliation, which may take 5-7 working days. Students need to collect the fee receipt in-person from the Cash Section, IIT Bombay for their record purpose.

Signed: Dy. Registrar HCU

=== NOTES APPLICABLE TO ALL FEE TABLES ===
1. Hostel Fees components are applicable only to students who have opted for hostel facilities. Charges will be NIL for those who have NOT opted for hostel facilities.
2. Academic fee payment is mandatory while paying the Hostel Fees.
3. Hostel Fees must be paid by 15.07.2026. After 15.07.2026, a fine of Rs.100/- per day w.e.f. 16.07.2026 will be charged till the date of payment. Request for a fine waiver will not be entertained.
4. Every UG student staying in the hostel has to pay a Per Semester Mess Advance (SMA). SMA can be paid in full or in two equal installments; the first installment is due by 15.07.2026 and the second by 30.09.2026. Late SMA payment is fined at Rs.100/- per day after the due date.
5. Married Ph.D students staying in quarters (MRSB / Tulsi / QIP, etc.) pay a License Fee as applicable under Estate Office rules.

HOSTEL ACCOMMODATION:
For students who are eligible for on-campus hostel accommodation, hostels are pre-allotted and communicated to students in advance. There are four hostels for male students (Hostel #17, Hostel #18, TANSA, Hostel #4) and three hostels for female students (Hostel #15, Hostel #10, Hostel #11).

New students report to their allotted hostel during specified reporting dates in office hours (10:00 am to 6:00 pm) and complete hostel occupation formalities. Temporary accommodation is provided if a student arrives outside office hours.

hours (10:00 am to 6:00 pm) and complete hostel occupation formalities. Temporary accommodation is provided if a student arrives outside office hours.

GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS FOR NEW ENTRANTS:
- Bring 5 passport-size photographs.
- Help desks are set up in each hostel where students submit a physical hard copy of the pre-filled hostel registration form and other necessary forms. After submission, students receive their hostel room keys.
- Help desks are also set up at the Main Gate of IIT Bombay to guide new students.

ROOM ALLOTMENT NOTE:
Rooms are double-occupancy rooms and students will have a room partner. Hostel authorities reserve the right to reshuffle rooms after the initial allotment to ensure consistent, uniform application of the double-occupancy policy during the student's first year.

ESSENTIALS AND MATTRESS STALLS:
Mattress stalls are available on campus where students can purchase essential items (mattress, pillow, pillow cover, bedsheets, bucket, mug, dustbins, etc.) at subsidized rates. These stalls are located at Hostel 17, Tansa, Hostel 15, and Hostel 10. Vendor contact details are displayed at various campus locations.

MESS ENROLLMENT:
Each hostel has its own mess. To enroll, students must contact the Mess Manager of their allotted hostel after completing hostel occupation formalities. Students must pay the Semester Mess Advance (SMA) and bring proof of payment to enroll in the mess facility.

completing hostel occupation formalities. Students must pay the Semester Mess Advance (SMA) and bring proof of payment to enroll in the mess facility.

SUPPORT:
The Institute Hostel Affairs Council and individual Hostel Councils provide assistance with hostel-related matters.

CONTACT ROLES (Hostel Affairs, illustrative structure — contact persons rotate each year):
- General Secretary Hostel Affairs (Institute-level)
- Institute Secretary Hostel Affairs (PG)
- Institute Secretary Hostel Affairs (UG) — multiple secretaries
- General Secretary for each individual hostel (e.g., Hostel 17, Hostel 18, Tansa & 4, Hostel 15, Hostel 11, Hostel 10)
- Warden Nominee for each hostel

For current-year contact names and phone numbers, students should check official hostel affairs communications sent at the start of the academic year, as these roles are re-elected annually.

11. BEHAVIOR: Misbehavior toward PHO (Public Health Office) workers, mess workers, office staff, security, or council members is not tolerated and is forwarded to the disciplinary committee.

HOSTELS AT IIT BOMBAY:
IIT Bombay has 17 hostels catering to student accommodation. Hostel Nos. 1 to 9, 12, 13, 14, and 15 (A and B wing) are for boys, while Hostel Nos. 10, 10A, 11, and 15 (C wing) are for girls.

COMMON FACILITIES IN EVERY HOSTEL:
- Washing and ironing facilities
- Computer room
- TV / common room
- Sports grounds
- Indoor games: Table Tennis, Carrom Board, Chess, etc.
- Access to most facilities is against the student's I-Card
- Internet connectivity in each room
- Several hostels have in-house shops for daily needs, stationery, xerox, and printing facilities

MESS / DINING:
Each hostel has its own mess, serving food four times a day (breakfast, lunch, snacks, dinner). Several additional food outlets are also spread around campus for students who wish to eat outside their hostel mess.

ROOM RETENTION DURING VACATIONS:
Students currently residing in hostels must follow room retention rules during vacations:
1. Students must submit a room retention form, duly signed by the respective authority, by the assigned date — 25th April for summer vacation, and an announced date for winter vacation.
2. If retention is not approved, the room must be vacated by the assigned date and keys handed over to the Hall Manager. Non-compliance incurs a fine of Rs.500/day.

FURTHER INFORMATION:
Details about individual hostels (specific amenities, hostel-level facilities, and hostel councils) are available via each hostel's own webpage on the Gymkhana portal. Hostel-specific queries should be directed to the respective hostel's General Secretary or Warden, while institute-wide hostel policy queries go to the Hostel Coordinating Unit (HCU) or Dean of Student Affairs (Dean SA).
